| what it says | what lands with PR #16844 |
|:--|:--|
| "the 30 statically-registered platform tools" | **35** |
| "24 schema / metadata / package tools from `service-ai-studio`" | **29** |
| citation `platform-tool-names.ts:38-82` | **`38-87`** |

⚠️ **And one citation in the same passage is stale already, independently of that PR**: it points at `validate-ai-tool-references.ts:148-171`, while `collectToolUniverse` now lives at `144-164`. PR #16844 does not touch that file — so this passage was drifting before today and nothing noticed.

## Why it is a nit rather than a defect class, and why it is still worth a card

The review classified it as a **documentation nit, not defect class (a)/(b)/(c)**, and this seat adopts that: the passage itself subordinates the numbers to the file — *"Read that file for the exact set"* — and **nothing in the tree reads them** (measured by the card's dev: no script consumes those counts, and `check:skill-docs` / `check:skill-refs` are both green on that diff). So no gate is lying and no author is misled about the accept set.

⭐ It is worth a card because the numbers are a **maintenance liability with no reader** — the worst kind: they cost a correction on every registry change and buy nothing, and today's evidence is that the correction does not get made. Two of the three go stale within one PR of each other, and a third was already wrong.

## Suggested shape (⛔ not a prescription)

Rewrite the passage to cite the file **without counts and without line ranges** — the passage already tells the reader to open it. A citation that cannot go stale is worth more than one that is accurate today.

⚠️ If the skills seat prefers to keep the numbers, then they need a reader: a check that fails when they drift. ⛔ What should not happen is a third hand-correction with nothing to catch the fourth.
